chunks.arabic_text: أَبَانُ بْنُ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ، وَاسَمُ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ: فِي رُزْ. تَابِعِيّ، رَوَى عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ. وَرَوَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, and the name of Abi Ayyash is Firuz. A tabi'i, he narrated from Anas ibn Malik. And he narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفٌ، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ. وَيُنْسَبُ أَصْحَابُنَا وَضْعَ "كِتَابِ سُلَيْمِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ" إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: Weak, he is not to be turned to. Our companions ascribe to him the fabrication of the book of Sulaym ibn Qays.

en.summary: Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, a tabi'i narrator known for transmitting from Anas ibn Malik and Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), is classified as weak (da'if) in Shia hadith sciences, leading scholars to discount his narrations. His association with the 'Book of Sulaym ibn Qays' highlights the historical debate regarding whether he was the original compiler or merely a transmitter of this important early Shia text.
en.seo_question: Who is Aban ibn Abi Ayyash and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.تَابِعِيّ: Tabi'i: A successor of the Companions of the Prophet
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak: A narrator whose reliability is not sufficient for establishing hadith
key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: Not to be turned to: A phrase indicating low reliability or that his narrations are not relied upon
key_terms.وَضْعَ: Fabrication/Attribution: The act of ascribing a work to someone
key_terms.كِتَابِ سُلَيْمِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ: The Book of Sulaym ibn Qays: A famous early Shia hadith book
